item.title: Russia's war in Ukraine: the situation
item.description:
Russian forces continue striking Ukrainian civilian targets, including a recent drone attack on an Oryol electronics plant and repeated strikes on Moscow-area airports, while Ukrainian forces have hit the same airports and targeted Russia's aviation sector. In occupied Oleshky, Melania Trump negotiated a local cease-fire that has reduced fighting, and a separate cease-fire was also agreed for the town. Ukraine reports that Starlink speed restrictions remain despite promises to restore service. The conflict caused 75,767 battle-related deaths in 2024, according to UCDP.

item.title: Israel, Gaza and the West Bank: the situation
item.description:
Israeli forces have expanded a lockdown of the occupied West Palestine and carried out home demolitions in Hebron after two Israeli soldiers were shot dead and two gunmen were killed. An Israeli airstrike hit a building in Nuseirat, Gaza, captured on video, while raids in Hebron detained dozens of Palestinians following the shooting attack. Prime Minister Netanyahu announced an extensive military operation and the closure of the West Bank in response to the Hebron attack. The conflict produced 21,440 battle-related deaths in 2024, according to UCDP.

item.title: Iran and the regional confrontation: the situation
item.description:
Iran has threatened to strike Gulf oil facilities, AI sites and undersea cables and reports seven ships hit in the Hormuz Strait, while Saudi Arabia’s King Fahd airport was hit by missiles, killing one person and wounding eight, prompting the United States to order its personnel to leave Saudi Arabia and advise diplomats to depart. Russian Foreign Minister Lavrov visited Tehran and publicly backed Iran, hinting at possible Russian involvement as the United States and Israel draft plans for renewed strikes after the US midterm elections. Saudi Arabia is expanding a missile plant that may produce more powerful missiles. 123 battle-related deaths occurred in 2024, according to UCDP.

item.title: Yemen and the Red Sea: the situation
item.description:
Houthi forces have intensified missile attacks on Saudi Arabia, striking Riyadh, Khamis Mushait, Dammam airport and an air base, while the Saudi-led coalition has repeatedly intercepted missiles and drones over Saudi territory. In Yemen, water supplies are dwindling in a city under Houthi siege and the UN warns that time is running out to reach Taiz as the crisis deepens. Oil prices have risen to a five-month high on fears of renewed US strikes on Iran and on Houthi attacks that disrupted crude markets. The conflict caused 918 battle-related deaths in 2024, according to UCDP.

item.title: Syria: the situation
item.description:
Israeli forces fired across the border into southern Syria, killing a Syrian man with disabilities in the Daraa buffer zone and deploying rooftop snipers who opened fire in the south. Two Syrian security officers were killed in a raid on an ISIL cell near Damascus. Hundreds of Syrians protested repeated Israeli incursions across the Syrian border. A Christian church in Jordan was shot, leaving at least seven dead and thirty-four injured, prompting Syrian condemnation and expanded talks in Aqaba. Trump promised to provide security for Kurds in Syria.

item.title: South Sudan: the situation
item.description:
Sudanese armed forces have continued drone strikes on markets in the disputed Abyei border region, killing more than 150 people in each attack. Communal clashes persist, with SSPDF and SPLA-IO forces fighting in Kapoeta North, Eastern Equatoria, and in Wij-Panyikang, Upper Nile, while a separate ambush killed two people in Kajo-Keji County. Monitors warned of rising violence ahead of December elections and reported 40,000 people displaced by renewed Upper Nile fighting. The UCDP recorded two battle-related deaths in 2024, according to UCDP.

item.description:
Ethiopian forces have installed a caretaker administration in Tigray and are moving toward the Eritrean border, while a pro-government militia says it seized the regional airport and reports Eritrean forces suffered losses there. The United States, through Secretary of State Marco Rubio, is urging Ethiopia and Eritrea to de-escalate, and Mekelle mayor Shishay Amare announced elections within six months to settle Western Tigray through constitutional processes. A drone strike in the disputed Abyei region killed at least 73 people. The conflict caused 2,824 battle-related deaths in 2024, according to UCDP.

item.description:

In northern Niger gunmen attacked buses, killing at least 12 people, and two European women were freed after kidnapping, while a US missionary held for nine months was released. Mali’s army and Russian fighters are also accused of new civilian abuses. The conflict produced 4,159 battle-related deaths in 2024, according to UCDP.

item.title: Nigeria: the situation
item.description:
Gunmen killed an NSCDC officer and abducted a businessman in Plateau despite a curfew, and gunmen attacked an Ebonyi assembly candidate convoy, killing one and injuring three. In Benue, suspected herders killed three civilians and Senate leaders are demanding a security overhaul and troop deployment after 113 people were killed, while electricity workers withdrew services in Makurdi following an alleged attack. Bandits continue to hold a widow, her son and a newborn captive three weeks after a kidnapping in Kaduna, and a NDC supporter was killed in Enugu. Floods killed 245 people and displaced over 200,000, according to NEMA, and the conflict produced 1,486 battle-related deaths in 2024, according to UCDP.

The Kuki-Zo Women’s forum called for President's Rule in Manipur, describing the crisis as political rather than security related. 437 battle-related deaths were recorded in 2024, according to UCDP.

Ethiopia has withdrawn more than 3,000 troops and will not intervene in the South West State conflict, while a UAE drone strike in Puntland killed four family members, including a pregnant teenager. item.title: Cameroon: the situation
item.description:
